newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat ready to meet Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Arafat ready to meet Netanyahu.

text.p: Yasser Arafat said in remarks broadcast on Friday in which he expressed sorrow at the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier that the most important thing now was to push peace moves forward.

Asked by Israel Radio if he would meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Palestinian president said in English: "I have no objection. The most important thing (is) how to push forward the peace process".

"I am very sorry for what had happened and I contacted his excellency the president and his excellency the prime minister and offered my condolences by the name of the Palestinian people," Arafat said, confirming reports he had telephoned Israel's President Ezer Weizman and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Arafat was speaking late on Thursday.
The telephone call to the prime minister was the first contact between the two leaders since Arafat last week angrily rejected a planned Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank.

Arafat aide Marwan Kanafani told Reuters on Thursday: "The president is willing to meet Netanyahu if the meeting is to discuss the latest Israeli measures, including the settlement in (Arab East Jerusalem) and (West Bank) redeployment."

Palestinian officials and Jordan's King Hussein had warned of the danger of bloodshed if Israel went ahead with plans to build 6,500 more homes for Jews between East Jerusalem and Bethlehem on land captured in 1967.
